itens.t: NASA's Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
itens.r: NASA's Voyager 1 has officially reached a staggering distance of one light-day from Earth, marking a historic milestone in interstellar exploration. The legendary spacecraft continues its unprecedented journey through the cosmos despite operating in the deep reaches of space for decades. Mission controllers celebrated the telemetry milestone at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California. The incredible achievement underscores the enduring legacy of humanity's farthest-flying machine.
itens.d:
NASA’s Voyager 1 probe has reached one light-day from Earth after more than 49 years of constant travel. The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST on November 18, 2026. Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory heard from the probe 24 hours later, matching the time required for its radio signal to reach Earth.

A light-day equals about 16.1 billion miles. Scientists use light to measure vast space distances, with light traveling at about 186,000 miles per second in a vacuum. Officials highlighted Voyager's dual legacy in planetary science and heliophysics missions offering insights into the Sun.
